label: the remaining matras: uu, o, au and the vocalic ri
note: All four are now drawn, and three of them were on the undrawn list only because nobody had checked which lesson was actually teaching them. The uu-maatraa was credited to HI-W06-name-sentence-stop, a lesson about the DANDA whose headword is puurna viraam; the o-maatraa to HI-W01-shirorekha-na-ma, a lesson about the HEAD-LINE whose headword is shirorekhaa (HL-C386). The au-maatraa had a real lesson already. The vocalic-r sign is the one that arrives ON TIME, at chapter 7, because its carrier ka is drawn at chapter 7 and its only headword kripayaa is at chapter 8 -- HL-C384 had wrongly listed it among glyphs that can never be on time, counting Sanskrit roots quoted in etymology notes as first use. The uu-maatraa is taught off its short twin (same hook, longer tail, longer vowel) and the o-maatraa off DO, one consonant and one mark, the plainest example in the language.
